CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Peterson is a 43-year-old patient who presents with right leg pain sustained during a bowling accident. While running up to the bowling lane with her ball held back, she swung it forward and struck her own right upper leg instead of the lane, causing her to fall. She reports minimal swelling but some bruising on the posterior aspect of the leg. She has difficulty walking and reports the leg is very sore. She notes she would avoid stairs if she had them. Currently self-treating with alternating ibuprofen and acetaminophen. On examination, she has significant tenderness over the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. She denies pain with hip or knee flexion/extension.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Focused on right leg pain; no other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema. Colectomy for diverticulitis.

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide for eczema as needed. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen alternating for pain management.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient bowls recreationally.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to palpation over lateral aspect of right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of right lower leg.

RESULTS
Right femur x-ray: Normal. No evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper leg contusion from blunt trauma. Started mobic 15 mg once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Ice for pain management. Expect improvement within one week. Patient to return if symptoms do not improve.
